source: Climate Resilient Broadcasting Rice Growing Technique, ASPIRE/IFAD, MAFF, Feb 2018
text:
Before sowing, test seed quality with a simple germination check (ការធ្វើតេស្តគ្រាប់ពូជ): take seed from three different spots in the bag, mix together, count out 100 seeds (including both full and empty-looking ones), repeat 3-5 times for a reliable sample, soak the sample in a bowl or basket, submerge under about 3cm of water, cover fully, and after 3 days count how many sprouted to estimate germination rate.

To clean seed before sowing, use the salt-water float test (ការសម្អាតគ្រាប់ពូជដោយប្រើទឹកអំបិល): pour seed into a container, add water and stir well, skim off any seed that floats to the surface since floating seed is typically empty or unfilled, then dissolve salt into the water (traditionally checked by floating a raw egg or duck egg in the brine until it floats) and pour the seed in again, continuing to skim off anything still floating, until only the good, dense, sinking seed remains at the bottom. Rinse the salt off the retained seed thoroughly with clean water before soaking it for sowing, since salt residue can damage germination.
